run.name: primary
run.title: Primary configuration: budgeted planning at matched damage.

interpretation: A failing check in the manuscript family is a discrepancy inside the article's own printed tables, not a defect in this release. Every execution-family quantity is the release's own on its release cohort, at the scale recorded above; the article's evaluation is a retrospective secondary analysis of trajectories it does not deposit.

manuscript_discrepancies.name: tier 1: uncertainty-propagation removal costs the printed information per unit damage
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: Sec. 3.4 states the cost is 0.026 nats per unit of damage

manuscript_discrepancies.name: tier 2 synergy: joint loss exceeds the sum of the two individual losses
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: Sec. 3.4 claims super-additivity on the transfer column

manuscript_discrepancies.name: sec 4: the Discussion's percentage increase equals the two printed coefficients
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: the Discussion describes the 0.289 to 0.487 move as a 75 percent increase

manuscript_discrepancies.name: abstract: the stable stratum's advantage matches Sec. 3.5
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: the abstract and Introduction print the stable stratum at zero while Sec. 3.5 prints 3.4

manuscript_discrepancies.name: sec 3.4: the prose leaves no symbol unfilled
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: Sec. 3.4 prints 'a loss of X for 6.5' and 'and Y in terms of 0.157'

manuscript_discrepancies.name: sec 4: an ordering-consistent stratum assignment reaches the printed frontier fit
manuscript_discrepancies.detail: Sec. 3.5 prints three of five stratum advantages and bounds the other two; the Discussion's slope, R-squared and interval must be reachable from an admissible assignment. The interval's half-width fixes the residual scale at about 0.08614 mean squared error, while the admissible stratum spread leaves at least 1.23; the printed fit therefore describes a tighter residual than the printed strata allow.
